name: SSH Brute-Force to Initial Access
description: Single attacker performs credential brute-force via SSH then achieves successful login.

ground_truth.annotator_notes: Classic SSH-Patator pattern ??? high packet rate to port 22, success implied by final low-flow connection.

name: Port Scan ??? Brute-Force ??? Exfiltration
description: Full 4-stage kill chain: reconnaissance, credential access, initial access, and data exfiltration.

ground_truth.annotator_notes: Textbook linear kill chain. Alert a002-3 (low bytes) signals successful login. Alert a002-4 is large HTTPS outbound ??? exfiltration.

name: DDoS Attack ??? Single Attacker
description: High-volume SYN flood targeting a single host ??? impact phase only.

ground_truth.annotator_notes: Short-duration ultra-high volume floods. Single-phase kill chain ??? Impact only. KCV will be very high.

name: Two Concurrent Attackers ??? Clustering Test
description: Two independent attackers active simultaneously. DBASC must split them into two sessions.

ground_truth.annotator_notes: Primary test for DBASC ??? must separate 10.1.0.10 and 172.31.0.20 into two distinct sessions despite interleaved timestamps.

name: Web Attack ??? XSS + SQL Injection
description: Attacker probes web application with XSS and SQL injection attempts.

ground_truth.annotator_notes: Low-volume but targeted web exploitation. XSS = probe/discovery, SQL Injection = exploitation attempt (Initial Access).

name: Bot / C2 Beacon Pattern
description: Compromised host beaconing to external C2 server at regular intervals.

ground_truth.annotator_notes: Regular 5-minute beacon intervals at constant low byte rate ??? textbook C2 keep-alive. Note: source IP is internal (compromised host).

name: FTP Brute-Force Only ??? Incomplete Chain
description: FTP-Patator attack with no evidence of successful login or subsequent activity.

ground_truth.annotator_notes: Partial chain ??? brute force with no observable success. Tests TKCI handling of single-phase sessions.

name: Infiltration ??? Dropbox Exfiltration
description: Attacker uses a legitimate cloud service (Dropbox-like) for covert data exfiltration.

ground_truth.annotator_notes: CICIDS 'Infiltration' label maps to exfiltration in ATT&CK context ??? large HTTPS transfer to known cloud storage IP range.

name: Three-Phase Attack ??? Recon + Exploit + C2
description: Attacker moves from discovery through initial access to establishing C2.

ground_truth.annotator_notes: Note IP pivot ??? a009-3 src is the victim host (now compromised), beaconing outbound. Tests multi-IP session handling.

name: DoS Goldeneye ??? Application-Layer Flood
description: Application-layer HTTP DoS attack against a web server.

ground_truth.annotator_notes: Application-layer flood at ~430K bytes/sec sustained. Single Impact phase. Very high KCV expected.

name: Heartbleed-Style Web Server Exploit
description: Attacker exploits a public-facing web application vulnerability and exfiltrates memory data.

ground_truth.annotator_notes: SQL injection achieves initial access to HTTPS server; immediate large outbound = data exfiltration.

name: Privilege Escalation via Brute Force + Sudo
description: SSH brute force followed by privilege escalation attempt on compromised host.

ground_truth.annotator_notes: a012-2 low bytes = successful login. a012-3 moderate traffic = privileged command execution.

name: Lateral Movement via SMB
description: Attacker moves laterally from an initially compromised host using SMB.

ground_truth.annotator_notes: Source is internal compromised host scanning SMB port on two additional internal hosts.

name: DoS Slowloris — Low-and-Slow HTTP Attack
description: Slow HTTP attack keeping many connections open to exhaust server resources.

ground_truth.annotator_notes: Low bytes/sec but very high packet count = Slowloris pattern. Tests KCV for slow-burn attacks.

name: XSS Probe + Credential Harvesting
description: Attacker uses XSS to steal session tokens followed by credential reuse.

ground_truth.annotator_notes: XSS = Initial Access exploit; subsequent HTTPS session = credential/token theft.

name: Three Attackers Concurrent — Maximum Clustering Test
description: Three attackers active simultaneously. DBASC must produce exactly 3 sessions.

ground_truth.annotator_notes: Primary test for 3-way DBASC separation. Interleaved timestamps every 60s. Each IP has a distinct attack type.

name: Bot Network — Periodic Beaconing with Data Staging
description: Compromised host beacons to C2 and then stages data before exfiltration.

ground_truth.annotator_notes: C2 beacons at 5-min intervals then large outbound at T+30 — data staged and exfilled via C2 channel.

name: FTP + SSH Sequential Brute Force — Same Target
description: Attacker tries FTP then pivots to SSH against the same target host.

ground_truth.annotator_notes: Same attacker, same destination, different port — DBASC must keep as one session. All Credential Access.

name: DoS LOIC HTTP — High Packet Rate Single Source
description: Low Orbit Ion Cannon HTTP flood — high packet rate from single source.

ground_truth.annotator_notes: Hulk DoS — HTTP GET flood to exhaust server. Very high KCV (2 phases in 60s).

name: Reconnaissance Only — No Follow-up Activity
description: Port scan with no subsequent exploitation — incomplete chain, CGAR must still retrieve recon context.

ground_truth.annotator_notes: Single-phase recon. CGAR must still return relevant MITRE docs. SI should be low.

name: Web Attack Brute Force Login
description: HTTP login page brute force attack using credential stuffing.

ground_truth.annotator_notes: HTTP brute force — credential stuffing. Maps to T1110.004 (Credential Stuffing).

name: Data Exfiltration via DNS Tunneling
description: Attacker uses DNS queries to exfiltrate data covertly in small UDP packets.

ground_truth.annotator_notes: UDP port 53 with high packet count but moderate bytes = DNS tunneling pattern. T1048.003.

name: Network Scan + Web Exploit + Persistence
description: Full 3-phase attack: recon, exploit public app, install persistence mechanism.

ground_truth.annotator_notes: Bot traffic after SQLi = web shell installed for persistence (T1505.003). Tests Recon→Access→Persist chain.

name: Two Attackers — Different Protocol Targets
description: Two attackers: one targets HTTP, another targets FTP. Simultaneous, different protocols.

ground_truth.annotator_notes: Tests DBASC on different dst_ip + different dst_port. Clear two-session output expected.

name: Collection — Keylogging / Screen Capture Simulation
description: Compromised host transmits small regular packets consistent with keylogger collection.

ground_truth.annotator_notes: Tiny but regular HTTPS traffic = keylogger exfil via C2 channel. Both Collection and C2 apply.

name: DoS GoldenEye + SSH Patator — Mixed Attack
description: Same attacker IP launches both DoS and SSH brute force against different targets.

ground_truth.annotator_notes: Same src_ip → one session despite different dst IPs. Tests DBASC IP weighting with multiple target hosts.

name: Slow Recon to Rapid Exploit — Time-Gap Test
description: Long time gap between reconnaissance and exploitation — tests DBASC temporal threshold.

ground_truth.annotator_notes: 90-minute gap between scan and brute-force. Tests whether DBASC temporal distance metric handles long gaps.

name: DoS RUDY Attack — Slow POST Body
description: R U Dead Yet slow-POST attack — very low bytes per packet over many packets.

ground_truth.annotator_notes: Near-zero bytes/packet ratio = RUDY. Low KCV (2 phases in 15 min). Low-and-slow impact.

name: Infiltration — Ares RAT Style Exfil
description: Compromised host contacts C2 then exfiltrates documents at irregular intervals.

ground_truth.annotator_notes: C2 beacon → collection pause → staged exfil in two bursts. Non-standard port 8080.

name: Full 5-Phase Kill Chain — Maximum Complexity
description: Complete advanced persistent threat simulation: recon → access → persistence → lateral → exfil.

ground_truth.annotator_notes: Maximum complexity APT scenario. IP pivot at a030-4 (victim becomes attacker for lateral/exfil). Tests full pipeline including TKCI chain ordering.

name: RDP Brute-Force Campaign
description: Mass RDP login attempts from external IP targeting Windows workstations.

ground_truth.annotator_notes: Single tactic — credential access via RDP brute-force.

name: SQL Injection → Data Exfiltration
description: Web attacker probes SQL injection then exfiltrates DB records via HTTP.

ground_truth.annotator_notes: Initial access via SQLi → exfiltration. CISA KEV hit on exfil alert.

name: Slowloris HTTP DoS
description: Application-layer DoS via Slowloris keeping HTTP connections open.

ground_truth.annotator_notes: Pure impact — sustained application DoS.

name: FTP Brute-Force
description: FTP-Patator credential stuffing on anonymous-disabled FTP server.

ground_truth.annotator_notes: Credential access via FTP brute-force.

name: XSS → Session Hijack
description: Stored XSS probe followed by account hijack via stolen session cookie.

ground_truth.annotator_notes: Web attack → credential theft via XSS.

name: ICMP Flood DDoS
description: Volumetric ICMP ping flood from multiple source IPs (distributed).

ground_truth.annotator_notes: 3 distinct source IPs → 3 sessions (DBASC IP mismatch). All impact.

name: Heartbleed Exploit Attempt
description: OpenSSL Heartbleed vulnerability exploitation on HTTPS server.

ground_truth.annotator_notes: CVE-2014-0160. CISA KEV. Low packet count but high severity due to memory disclosure.

name: Bot C2 Beacon
description: Compromised host beaconing to known botnet C2 at regular intervals.

ground_truth.annotator_notes: Regular 5-min C2 beacon over HTTPS. Low KCV but persistent.

name: DNS Tunneling Exfiltration
description: Data exfiltration encoded in DNS TXT queries to attacker-controlled domain.

ground_truth.annotator_notes: DNS tunneling → exfiltration. High bytes-per-packet ratio is key signal.

name: GoldenEye HTTP DoS
description: GoldenEye tool creating persistent HTTP keepalive connections to exhaust server threads.

ground_truth.annotator_notes: Impact only. GoldenEye HTTP keepalive flood.

name: Dual Attacker: Brute-Force + DDoS Simultaneous
description: Two simultaneous attackers: attacker A SSH brute-force, attacker B UDP flood. Tests DBASC 2-session separation.

ground_truth.annotator_notes: Core DBASC test: 2 attacker IPs → 2 sessions. SI_B > SI_A due to impact tactic.

name: Recon → Lateral Movement → Ransomware
description: Full APT kill chain: port scan → credential theft → lateral movement → ransomware deployment.

ground_truth.annotator_notes: 4-tactic chain. CISA KEV on exfil. Longest chain in dataset — tests TKCI ordering.

name: Web Shell Upload → Persistence
description: Attacker exploits file upload to place PHP web shell, then establishes persistence via scheduled task.

ground_truth.annotator_notes: Web shell persistence then outbound exfil. Victim IP becomes source in alert 3.

name: Log4Shell Exploitation
description: CVE-2021-44228 Log4Shell RCE via LDAP callback, followed by reverse shell.

ground_truth.annotator_notes: Log4Shell. CVE-2021-44228 CISA KEV. Victim becomes C2 client in alerts 2-3.

name: Credential Dump → Pass-the-Hash
description: Credential access via LSASS dump, then lateral movement via pass-the-hash to admin shares.

ground_truth.annotator_notes: SMB lateral movement post-credential-dump. Same src_ip → 1 session.

name: Three Concurrent Attack Vectors
description: Three simultaneous attackers: A=DDoS, B=SSH-Patator, C=Web-XSS. Tests DBASC with 3 sessions.

ground_truth.annotator_notes: 3 IPs → 3 sessions. Tests DBASC with eps=0.35. All concurrent.

name: Supply Chain: Trojanised Update → C2 → Exfil
description: Software update channel compromised, delivers backdoor that beacons C2 then exfiltrates source code.

ground_truth.annotator_notes: Supply-chain persistence → C2 beacon → bulk exfil. CISA KEV on exfil.

name: Insider Threat: Privilege Escalation + Data Staging
description: Internal user escalates privileges then stages sensitive data for exfiltration.

ground_truth.annotator_notes: Insider. Internal escalation → data staging → cloud upload.

name: Botnet Recruit: Scan → Exploit → Install
description: Automated botnet scanner finds vulnerable service, exploits it, installs bot agent.

ground_truth.annotator_notes: Fully automated: scan → exploit → C2 in 60 seconds. High KCV expected.

name: APT28-Patterned Multi-Stage Campaign
description: Full APT campaign: recon, spear-phishing probe, credential access, lateral movement, C2, exfil over 2 hours.

ground_truth.annotator_notes: Maximum complexity. 6-tactic chain over 2.5 hours. KCV=2.4 → manual/APT. CISA KEV on exfil. Tests full TKCI + CGAR + PFGL pipeline.
